Alex Gomez: Hi all, first week Q: I'm trying to run an integration that hits streaming endpoints to validate latency from my devbox. Should I use my hosted key or the sandbox key for this? I want realistic behavior but don't want to burn onboarding credits.
Rina Singh: Welcome Alex! Usually sandbox is safe for dev, but note sandbox models are sometimes smaller/older and streaming performance can differ. If you need production-like kernels/latency, ask for a short hosted window.
Alex Gomez: Got it. How do I prove it's safe? I can limit test to a single IP and a narrow time window.
Ibrahim Khan: If you want hosted for a smoke, ops can create a time-limited ephemeral quota tied to your key and/or your dev IP. Ops prefers a ticket with: duration, expected qps, whether streaming and model name.
Alex Gomez: Where do I file that ticket?
Rina Singh: File to ops-team@redwood.ai or use the internal portal. If you need a faster reply, ping @Ibrahim Khan here after filing.
Alex Gomez: Filed OPS-4901 with: "2026-03-24 18:30-18:45 UTC, ~200 requests total, streaming, model: redwood-medium". Pinged Ibrahim.
Ibrahim Khan: Received. I'll attach an IP whitelist for your devbox if you give the public IP. Also note that streaming connections count against concurrency buckets differently; we may route you to a lower-cost compatible variant if cost is a concern.
Alex Gomez: Public IP is 34.102.54.11. Thanks. One more: how can I tell if my key is hosted vs sandbox from the CLI?
Rina Singh: There's a simple call to the keys endpoint:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/me | jq .key_type
```
It returns "hosted" or "sandbox".
Alex Gomez: Sweet. Also want to simulate rate limits locally so CI behaves correctly. Any recommended approach?
Ibrahim Khan: Best is to run a local throttle that returns 429s at desired QPS using our testing helper. For quick tests, add this header to emulate a 429 after N requests: `X-Test-Force-429: 5` (the backend test proxy will return a 429 on the 5th request). Don't rely on it for perf benchmarks though.
Alex Gomez: Nice. Is there a recommended backoff policy for clients?
Rina Singh: Exponential backoff with jitter. Example: base=100ms, factor=2, max=2500ms, random jitter +-30%. Works well for CI.
Billing Bot: Reminder: hosted windows outside onboarding credits will charge. OPS tickets should include billing owner or manager approval if >$50 estimated.
Alex Gomez: My manager confirmed onboarding credits cover this one. Thanks for the tip.
Ticket Bot: OPS-4901 status: queued -> approved by Ibrahim Khan. Whitelist applied for IP 34.102.54.11, window 2026-03-24 18:30-18:45 UTC.
Alex Gomez: Amazing, testing later today. Appreciate the quick help everyone :clap:
